newsitem.title: SPAIN: Man who killed two Basque police to walk free.
newsitem.headline: Man who killed two Basque police to walk free.

text.p: A man who shot dead two Basque police officers in northern Spain two years ago was acquitted of murder in a San Sebastian court on Thursday after a trial steeped in controversy.

The court said the jury of eight women and one man acquitted Mikel Otegi, 23, on the basis that he was not responsible for his actions when he shot two officers dead with a shotgun at a farm in Itsasondo in northern Spain in 1995.

Otegi had used the fact that he had suffered a mental blackout at the time of the murders as part of his defence, local media said. He was suspected of being a member of the radical youth group Jarrai which has links to Basque separatist group ETA.
The verdict sent shock waves through political circles and the Spanish government said it would do what it could to try to reverse the verdict.

"We will apply whatever methods of recourse are available to make sure this verdict does not stick and we achieve a different result from the nonsense we have here," Interior Minister Jaime Mayor Oreja told local television.

Local media said the court had had trouble putting together a jury for the trial as potential jurors feared becoming ETA targets. The court said the jurors had requested that their names be expunged from the records.
Oreja said the verdict illustrated the problems associated with trials by jury, a relatively new concept in Spain's judicial system.
"It is very clear that such risky experiments will give the results we have here..the most important thing is that this type of situation is not repeated," he said.
Otegi was expected to be freed on Thursday evening, local radio said.
